Alcoholic liver disease, hepatitis, or carbon tetrachloride poi-
soning can result in abnormal triglyceride deposits (fatty liver). 
Th e abnormal fat and protein deposits within arterial walls
of the circulatory system characterize the common chronic 
disease atherosclerosis.
A common cellular response to injury and disease is deposi-
tion of a substance called hyaline within and between the cells. 
Most hyaline deposits are a mixture of diﬀ erent types of pro-
teins such as collagen, ﬁ brin, and amyloid. Hyaline deposits 
can be found in many diﬀ erent cell types including neurons,
hepatocytes, and cells in damaged arteries. Th e predominant 
type of protein within the hyaline accumulation can vary 
depending on the individual disease process. Fibrin masses are
